analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy
key_insights: Major Asian tech sell-off overnight on Chinese AI competition concerns: KOSPI -6.30% (two-day drop of -9.79%, largest since July), Nikkei 225 -2.21% on return from a long weekend.

Catalyst was a South China Morning Post report that China's CXMT made progress on a new DRAM architecture that would boost memory density. Micron fell -3.88% yesterday, Samsung -7.98% and SK Hynix -8.72% this morning.

Philly semiconductor index fell -2.67% yesterday, its 4th consecutive daily decline and the first such streak since July. Two-thirds of the index was higher and the Mag-7 closed +0.47%. Nasdaq futures are -0.79% this morning, S&P and Stoxx futures about -0.19%.

US Q3 earnings season starts today with JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo and Citigroup, followed tomorrow by Bank of America, Morgan Stanley and BlackRock. Financials are expected to have among the weakest YoY growth of any sector.
DB US equity strategists expect S&P 500 Q3 earnings growth of 34% YoY (a record) versus consensus at 27%, arguing consensus embeds too much of a slowdown and leaves scope for above-average beats.
DB equity strategists expect European Q3 earnings growth of 25%, 5 pp above consensus. European season kicks off next week.
Brent closed up +1.84% at about $106/bbl and fell -1.12% in Asia this morning. European natural gas futures rose +3.58% to a post-2022 high of EUR84.24/MWh.

Energy prices were lifted by the weekend report that Houthi militants bombed Riyadh's airport, doubt over a Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire (Zelenskyy said Ukraine would respond if Russia did not agree), and nervousness about a wider Middle East escalation.
Euro 1yr inflation swaps rose +4.7bps to 3.52%, pushing front-end yields higher across Europe. The 2yr yield rose in Germany (+2.4bps), France (+1.5bps) and Italy (+2.3bps).

The Franco-German 10yr spread widened +5.1bps to 142bps, a post-2012 high, with less market stress than when 2012 levels were first breached 10 days ago. French front-end bonds did not underperform, which may suggest summer front-end carry positions have been squared.
US bond markets were closed yesterday for a holiday. 10yr US yields are down -4.6bps this morning.
S&P 500 closed -0.06%, STOXX 600 +0.65%, DAX +0.76%, CAC 40 +0.38%. European indices closed higher despite higher gas prices.

JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo and Citigroup report Q3 results today (Oct 14). Bank of America, Morgan Stanley and BlackRock report tomorrow. No results are reported in this note.
